title: Canva’s first AI image model plans designs before generating them
slides: Canva built an AI that plans before it draws?
It first sketches a layout, then generates images inside it
Most image models ignore design structure entirely
Your rough Canva prompts may now produce usable layouts
Test one real brief and compare output
thread_text:
1. Most image AI ignores design

Canva's new model plans the layout first, then generates images to fit. That's the opposite of how most tools work.

2. Sketch before you draw

It starts with a rough layout sketch, then fills in the visuals. This mirrors how a human designer would approach a blank page.

3. Your prompts get smarter

Because the AI handles structure, even a vague Canva prompt can now produce a usable layout—no more fighting with broken compositions.

4. Structure changes everything

Without a planned layout, generated images often clash with your text and branding. Canva's approach solves that by designing the container first.

5. Test it on a real brief

Take one actual project and compare Canva's output to your usual process. Does it save time or just shift the editing work? Try it today.

instagram.caption:
Canva's new AI model sketches a layout before it generates a single image.

Most image models ignore design structure entirely—they just fill a prompt with visuals and hope the composition holds.

Canva's approach is closer to how a human designer works: rough layout first, visuals second. 🎨

That means even a vague prompt can now produce a usable layout, with images that fit your text and branding instead of clashing with them.

If you publish anything—posts, decks, flyers—this could cut the back-and-forth of fixing broken compositions. ✂️

Take one real brief this week and compare Canva's output to your usual process. Does it save time, or just shift the editing work? 🤔
